items: Difficulty numbers are redone again with a more careful rater: every question was rated three times and the ratings averaged, easy questions are no longer stuck at 0, and most questions are now between about 1 and 4.5.
Difficulty numbers are finer: they're no longer only whole and half points (each question's ratings are combined into one number).

Difficulty numbers are redone: every question was rated by reading it, and a number now says about how many teams would get it (5 is about 1 team in 10, 10 about 1 in 100). Routine calculations no longer look hard and easy facts on fancy-sounding topics no longer look niche. Most questions are now between 0 and 4.
Practice: a Give up button (or press G) shows the answer without moving on; press Next when you're ready. The save star now lines up with the text beside it.

Rooms on phones: the room bar is one short line (code, Invite, Chat, Leave); Chat opens over the game and shows how many new messages there are; the scores are right under the question. If your phone can't read aloud (or your voice is off), the question's words now appear as the host's voice reads them instead of all at once, and the note about it is one small line.

Better on computers: the buzzer stays in the same place for almost every question, the top bar lines up with the page, the Questions page filters are a tidy grid, Help has an "On this page" list beside it, and pressing ? on any page shows the keyboard shortcuts (/ jumps to the search box on the Questions page).

Better on phones: the tabs are now a bar at the bottom of the screen (all six always visible, and the top bar is one line), the buzzer and Next / Skip / Pause always sit in the same place at the bottom of the screen however long the question is, the answer scrolls into view when it's shown, and the Questions page filters are two to a row.

Questions page: a Sort by menu (easiest or hardest first, newest or oldest set, set name, subject), with a ⇅ button to step through the orders. The Saved only box is gone; saved questions are on the Saved page. The difficulty chart is shorter.
The Difficulty slider on the Questions page now shows a small chart of how many questions there are at each difficulty (for the other filters you picked), with the range you pick in gold.
While a question is being read, its set, round and number stay hidden; they show once the question is over, along with its difficulty.
Removed the 45 Princess Anne joke questions (Roundshare 2024, Princess Anne Round 2).
Questions page: a Difficulty slider with two handles shows only questions in a difficulty range (say 6 to 8, or 9 and up).

Difficulty numbers are much more accurate: they now follow how niche the topic and the answer are and how much a calculation takes, not how long or flashy a question is (fitted to hand ratings of 444 questions). They're shown as a plain gold number everywhere. A typical question is now about 3.7, and 8 and up is reserved for very hard specialist questions.

Every question now has a difficulty number from 0 to 10 (the hardest go past 10; 5 is typical), shown after the question is read and on the Questions and Saved pages. Sets and rounds get the average of their questions, shown in the Packets list and the Set and Round filters. Help → Difficulty explains how it's worked out.
Questions page: click a question's set and round ("MIT 2025, Round 3, #12") to see that whole round in order, opened at that question.
The online count now counts people, not tabs: several tabs open on the same network count once.

Search Google now searches the whole question: text in square brackets (like the interval [0,2]) and math such as ln, fractions and roots were sometimes left out, and very long questions were cut short.

Cleaned up about 700 questions: leftover writer tags, packet notes and "End of packet" text taken out of answers; multiple-choice answers now match the choice that's read (about 35 had the wrong letter, like the U-238 decay question); repeated or garbled choices fixed (Excel had turned fractions like 3/4 into dates); power marks (*) removed from NSBA and MOSFET 2021; a few short answers that were really multiple choice now show W–Z buttons; 11 duplicate or unanswerable questions removed.

41 more questions and 27 more visual bonuses with their pictures, from questions the packet reader had skipped or misnumbered (SMH 2026, NSBA 2022/2023, CSBL, CAST 2021, Roundshare 2024, BASED 2025, BASH, WSBT 2023, CLASH 2026 and others). 38 questions that were filed under the wrong number, round or type (a bonus saved as a toss-up, say) now sit in the right place, so toss-ups and bonuses pair up correctly.
Fixed 1 question (DASONI 2 2025).

Every question now shows its ID (like "ID 1qy21vz") on the Questions and Saved pages and in your session history. Type an ID in the Questions page search to jump straight to that question, e.g. to report it or send it to a friend.
21 more questions (Roundshare 2024, Lexington 2021, MHS 2020, NNHS 2021, SCB 2025, MOSFET 2024, NSI 2023, SBST Spring), fixed up by hand from questions the packet reader had left out.

Rooms: when someone gets a question wrong, their answer stays under the answer box (with who said it and whether it was a neg) until the next question, so it doesn't vanish when the next person buzzes.

Visual bonuses with several parts are much easier to answer: type the parts in order with commas, semicolons, spaces or labels like "1) … 2) …" ("h, m, pearlite" works for "1) H; 2) M; 3) Pearlite"), and a wrong answer says which parts you got right.
65 more visual bonuses (DASONI 2, ESBOT, WISC, NSBA1, SMH 2024 and others) now show their pictures. They were in the question bank without them.
Lexington 2021 Round 8 #11 (toss-up and bonus) and two Round 5 geometry questions have their missing numbers and math back.

Fixed the reported questions: 244 questions that showed their W/X/Y/Z choices as a short answer are now multiple choice, and 68 answers no longer end in stray words like "Halftime" or "Visual Bonus" (so "Huygens" and "summer triangle" count again).
Questions like "Of the following, which are..." with a numbered list now get number buttons on phones and tablets.
On phones and tablets, tap the answer box to buzz.
Reading speed (on-screen mode) now goes from 250 to 1000 words per minute.
Help → Without internet now shows whether pts is fully saved for offline use, with a progress count while it saves.
pts now works without internet once it has loaded. On an iPhone or iPad, add it to your home screen (Share → Add to Home Screen) and open it once online; after that it works anywhere.

41 more questions (NSBA2 2023, NSBA1 2022, AVES 2026, BASED 2025, BTHS 2025, DASONI Standard 2022, HSBT 2026, Discord Summer 2019, ICSBT3 2026, LOST1 2020, NWI 2024), fixed up by hand from questions the packet reader had left out.
Removed 3 broken questions (SMH 2024).
1 more question (Roundshare 2024), fixed up by hand from questions the packet reader had left out.
44 more questions (CSBL, Lexington 2021, MIT 2021, Prometheus 2022, ICSBT3 2026, ICSBT1 2024, MIT 2020, MIT 2022, NSI2 2024), fixed up by hand from questions the packet reader had left out.
5 more questions (CSBL, CAST 2021), fixed up by hand from questions the packet reader had left out.

70 more questions (Roundshare 2024, Clements 2025, DASONI 2 2025, MOSFET 2024, NOHO Scrim, SMH 2024, DASONI Standard 2022, DAST 2024, DVMS 2025, Deadbird, HSBT 2026, Lexington 2021, MHS 2020, MOOSE, NSI2 2024, WISC, DASONI Competitive 2022, Enloe 2022, ICSBT1 2024, ICSBT2 2025, MNSBT 2024, NWI 2024, Pokahu 2024, SSBT, WSBT 2023, SBST Spring), fixed up by hand from questions the packet reader had left out.
On phones and iPads, "identify all" and ordering questions have number buttons: tap the numbers (in order, for ordering) and press Submit. Nothing picked answers "None".
The buzzer stays in one place while a question is read instead of sliding down as more words appear.
"None" now counts for answers written "None of them" or "Neither", and "identify all" lists written on one line (I) ... II) ...) are checked as lists.
Ordering questions: the direction words (increasing, decreasing, lowest to highest, first to last...) are in bold so they're hard to miss.
On phones and iPads, multiple choice has W X Y Z buttons to tap instead of typing.

Report: something wrong with a question (answer, typo, broken math, a ruling)? Press Report after the answer, in your session history, or on the Questions and Saved pages, and say what's wrong. No account needed.
Read aloud: the buzzer now starts when the voice finishes the question, not a moment before.
12 more questions (CSBL, BASED 2025, AVES 2024, BASH, BTHS 2025, CAST 2021, CLASH 2026, CLASH MS 2026, CSBL 2), fixed up by hand from questions the packet reader had left out.
Visual bonuses now give you 30 seconds (Timing and scoring has the setting), and Questions → Visual bonuses only practices just them.

Visual bonuses: 294 bonuses that come with a picture (a diagram, graph, structure or photo) from 22 tournaments, including the ones whose pictures were in a separate slide deck. The picture shows as soon as the bonus starts, also when questions are read aloud, like the handout in a real round; click it to see it bigger. They're on by default: untick Visual bonuses in the settings to leave them out. On the Questions page, Type → Visual bonus shows only these.
Fixed an ICSBT 1 2024 ocean-models question whose correct answer was marked wrong (the answer was stuck in choice Z).

Math in about 530 questions was fixed: exponents that had been flattened (x6 for x to the sixth), limits, integrals and sums, square and cube roots, towers like 3 to the 3 to the 3, and chemical formulas whose subscripts had come apart. Subscripts and charges now sit right against their formula (CO₂, not CO ₂), dollar amounts no longer turn into math, and Listen mode reads fractions, roots, limits and integrals the way a moderator would.

Subcategories: in Settings under Subjects, pick parts of a subject to practice (Genetics, Anatomy & Physiology, Optics, Calculus, Organic, Astronomy...), for Science Bowl and Ocean Science Bowl. The Questions page can filter by them too. Packets don't print these, so they were worked out from each question's wording and a few will be off.
WISC questions no longer end with the writer's initials ("[SA]", "[JI]"); they're in the question's notes. Two WISC chemistry questions with garbled formulas were fixed.
The top bar shows how many people are on pts right now.

574 questions no longer start with leftovers from their packets: the round number in brackets ("[11]", all of MOSFET 2021), empty brackets, or notes to the reader like "[read slowly]" (now in the question's notes).
Read aloud: the buzz timer starts as the last word ends, not a beat later, and buzzing on the last word no longer counts as a neg.
Rooms: devices on networks that block direct connections (school Wi-Fi, WARP, school Chromebooks) now connect through a relay server.
Rooms: when a network blocks the connection between devices (school Wi-Fi, VPNs like WARP), joining now says so instead of "No room found", and the site can use a relay server to get through.
Ocean Science Bowl: 1,759 more questions from regional bowl teams (Blue Heron Bowl, Lake Sturgeon Bowl) and a 2017 NOSB practice set.
Read aloud: degrees are read as degrees ("25 degrees Celsius", and "naught" for ΔH°), and ion charges as charges ("Fe 3 plus", "CO 3 2 minus") instead of "to the".

Read aloud: when a question says how to read an equation or formula ("[READ: x squared plus y squared …]"), the voice reads that instead of the symbols; reader notes like "[read slowly]" are no longer read out.
Read aloud: words are said as written again, and printed pronunciation guides are skipped, since some voices were spelling the respellings out letter by letter.
Read aloud: shorter pauses between multiple-choice options.

Read aloud: pronunciation guides are reworded so voices don't spell out pieces like "sih" (siliceous) or garble endings (achondroplasia); words on the site's pronunciation list now win over a packet's guide.
Help: this changelog.
Rooms: a player whose device doesn't have the host's voice now has it sped up or slowed down to keep the host's pace.
Read aloud: hard terms are said from the packet's own pronunciation guide, or from a list of about 260 respelled scientific names and terms.
Stats: a toss-up attempts bar (correct, wrong, negs), points per toss-up by subject, and buzz point by subject.
A Search Google button after each question, searching the whole question and its answer choices.
Wrong early buzzes are called negs, as in real Science Bowl.
Answer checking: answers with variables are compared by value (1/4 omega matches ω/4), and LaTeX degree signs are understood.
Stats: recent questions show their set, round and number.
4,529 questions added: MOOSE, NCB 2026, Lexington Biology Bowl 2026, the 2023-24 Roundshare and more. LOST2 removed, since its scanned packet couldn't be read reliably.
Answer checking: numbered statements can be answered by name, the question's noun can be left off (O for "what horizon"), and a different number is never a typo.
Questions search: fixed highlighting on long searches.

Read aloud became listen mode: the question is only heard, and its text shows after. Short pauses before answer choices; in rooms the host picks one voice for everyone; voices no longer stop mid-word.
Ocean Science Bowl: an SB / OSB switch with 801 NOSB questions.
8,841 questions from 18 more tournaments.
Random order spreads questions evenly across the six main subjects.
Room settings are remembered between rooms; a home-screen icon for iPhone.
Questions tab: easier paging, and the round filter lists every round of the picked set.
Rooms: a ping badge; ruling an earlier buzz correct voids later buzzes.
15,888 questions from 33 more tournaments.
Each question starts with its subject and type; Roman-numeral lists accept numbers.
Filter by round stage: round robin, early, mid or late double elimination.
An IsoBowl-style scoreboard.
Saved questions (bookmarks), lenient "all" answers, and math answers compared by value.
13,588 questions from MIT, Stanford, Texas, MOSFET and 20 more tournaments; large banks load fast.
